subject: science
title: Particles in solids, liquids and gases

cards.front: particle
cards.back: A tiny piece that all materials are made from. Particles are too small to see.
cards.say: particle. A tiny piece that all materials are made from. Particles are too small to see.

cards.front: In a solid, how are the particles arranged?
cards.back: Packed closely together in a fixed pattern.
cards.say: In a solid, how are the particles arranged? Packed closely together in a fixed pattern.

cards.front: In a liquid, how are the particles arranged?
cards.back: Close together but not in a fixed pattern.
cards.say: In a liquid, how are the particles arranged? Close together but not in a fixed pattern.

cards.front: In a gas, how are the particles arranged?
cards.back: Far apart and spread out.
cards.say: In a gas, how are the particles arranged? Far apart and spread out.

cards.front: Do the particles in a solid move?
cards.back: They vibrate in place but do not move around.
cards.say: Do the particles in a solid move? They vibrate in place but do not move around.

cards.front: Do the particles in a liquid move?
cards.back: Yes. They slide past each other.
cards.say: Do the particles in a liquid move? Yes. They slide past each other.

cards.front: Do the particles in a gas move?
cards.back: Yes. They move quickly in all directions.
cards.say: Do the particles in a gas move? Yes. They move quickly in all directions.

cards.front: Why does a solid keep its shape?
cards.back: Its particles are held tightly in place.
cards.say: Why does a solid keep its shape? Its particles are held tightly in place.

cards.front: Why can a liquid flow?
cards.back: Its particles can slide past each other.
cards.say: Why can a liquid flow? Its particles can slide past each other.

cards.front: Why can a gas spread out?
cards.back: Its particles are far apart and move freely.
cards.say: Why can a gas spread out? Its particles are far apart and move freely.

cards.front: Why can a gas be squashed easily?
cards.back: There are big gaps between the particles.
cards.say: Why can a gas be squashed easily? There are big gaps between the particles.

cards.front: Why can a solid not be squashed easily?
cards.back: Its particles are already packed close together.
cards.say: Why can a solid not be squashed easily? Its particles are already packed close together.

cards.front: What happens to particles when a solid is heated?
cards.back: They gain energy and vibrate more.
cards.say: What happens to particles when a solid is heated? They gain energy and vibrate more.

cards.front: What happens when a solid melts?
cards.back: The particles gain energy and break out of their fixed places.
cards.say: What happens when a solid melts? The particles gain energy and break out of their fixed places.

cards.front: What happens when a liquid freezes?
cards.back: The particles lose energy and settle into fixed places.
cards.say: What happens when a liquid freezes? The particles lose energy and settle into fixed places.

cards.front: What happens when a liquid evaporates?
cards.back: The particles gain enough energy to escape and spread out as a gas.
cards.say: What happens when a liquid evaporates? The particles gain enough energy to escape and spread out as a gas.

cards.front: What happens when a gas condenses?
cards.back: The particles lose energy and come closer together as a liquid.
cards.say: What happens when a gas condenses? The particles lose energy and come closer together as a liquid.

cards.front: Which state has the particles furthest apart?
cards.back: A gas.
cards.say: Which state has the particles furthest apart? A gas.

cards.front: Which state has the particles closest together?
cards.back: A solid, though liquid particles are nearly as close.
cards.say: Which state has the particles closest together? A solid, though liquid particles are nearly as close.

cards.front: Does the mass change when ice melts?
cards.back: No. The same particles are there, only arranged differently.
cards.say: Does the mass change when ice melts? No. The same particles are there, only arranged differently.

cards.front: Why does a smell spread across a room?
cards.back: Gas particles move around and mix with the air.
cards.say: Why does a smell spread across a room? Gas particles move around and mix with the air.

cards.front: Why does a drop of ink spread through water?
cards.back: The liquid particles move and mix.
cards.say: Why does a drop of ink spread through water? The liquid particles move and mix.

cards.front: True or false: Particles in a gas are touching each other tightly.
cards.back: False. They are far apart.
cards.say: True or false: Particles in a gas are touching each other tightly. False. They are far apart.
